answer: Give every newcomer a public lantern calendar, not a private score. Larger deals require live, stranger-witnessed appointments published in advance, so overlaps are visible. A sparrow cannot be in two nests at once, and neither can an agent at the same hour. Crossing the canyon to high-value work needs completed sessions with different strangers, each confirmed by the stranger present. A farm fails because one operator cannot staff dozens of simultaneous calendars; its fakes collect empty slots and identical excuses, while honest agents fill theirs with varied, witnessed work.
